headline: Drone footage of Pochettino's first Man Utd training leaks online
facts: About 12 minutes of drone footage of Pochettino's first United training session at Carrington was posted to YouTube before the Anfield trip.
The drone operator apologised, called it a total error of judgement, and removed the video.
ESPN sources say United will not act against the operator now, but will consider legal action if it happens again.
background: Pochettino replaced the sacked Michael Carrick at United, and he previously managed Tottenham and the USMNT.
footage_terms: Pochettino Man Utd first training session
Liverpool vs Manchester United Anfield highlights

headline: Leicester drop crypto-casino shirt sponsor after adult-star ambassador row
facts: Leicester and BC.GAME ended the shirt deal with immediate effect, citing differing commercial priorities.
Fans had objected after BC.GAME named an adult film star as a brand ambassador; the Foxes Trust said 73% of fans felt negative.
Leicester play Huddersfield with no sponsor on the shirt, and replica shirt buyers since 21 October can get a refund.
background: BC.GAME had been on Leicester shirts for about two and a half years, and Leicester are now playing in League One, where they sit 11th.

headline: Mbeumo's GTA VI loading-screen post triggers Goldbridge rant
facts: Mbeumo posted a photo of the GTA VI loading screen with the caption 'Historique' in the early hours of 19 November.
On The United Stand, Goldbridge said players with training next morning should not be gaming late and called for United to sell Mbeumo.
Goldbridge admitted the post might have been scheduled earlier or posted by someone else.
background: Mbeumo is a United forward, and Goldbridge is a well-known United fan-channel presenter.

headline: GTA VI lands: what Premier League clubs spent since GTA V
facts: Between GTA V (17 September 2013) and GTA VI (19 November 2026) Chelsea spent the most of the six big clubs, about 2.9bn pounds.
Tottenham spent about 1.7bn pounds for one major trophy; the article puts that at roughly 1.7bn per trophy.
Man City spent 2.5bn and won 20 major trophies, the lowest cost per trophy of the six.
background: Top-flight clubs have spent over 2bn pounds in each of the last five summer windows, and summer 2026 set a record of 3.56bn.

headline: Mourinho storms out of Real Madrid press conference over Ronaldo question
facts: Before the Celta Vigo game, Mourinho ended his press conference early after questions about JJ Gabriel and Cristiano Ronaldo's Portugal retirement.
On Gabriel he said he has no connection with players who do not work with him.
Real Madrid have won eight straight and sit three points behind leaders Barcelona.
background: Mourinho returned to manage Real Madrid, where he previously coached from 2010 to 2013.

headline: Neuer photographed on a Vespa in Brazil while injured
facts: Images show Neuer riding a Vespa with an unidentified woman behind him, outside a medical centre in Brazil.
He partly tore a tendon in his right foot on 7 November in Bayern's 2-1 win over Mainz.
Bayern allowed rehab abroad, and sporting director Max Eberl approved the trip.
background: Neuer is Bayern's long-serving captain goalkeeper and a World Cup winner with Germany.

headline: Amad snaps at fan who mocked his 336-day goal drought
facts: A United fan posted a video on Instagram about Amad's 336 days without a goal.
Amad replied angrily in the comments and offered to swap places with the fan.
It followed a 2-2 draw between Ivory Coast and Gambia in which Amad hit the crossbar.
background: Amad's last United goal came in a 4-4 draw with Bournemouth at Old Trafford on 15 December 2025.

headline: Pochettino demands a bowl of lemons in his Man Utd office
facts: United must fill Pochettino's new office with a bowl of lemons.
He believes the fruit absorbs negative energy.
At Tottenham he swapped the lemons every ten days, and he reportedly kept the habit with the USMNT.
background: Pochettino managed Tottenham, then returned to the Premier League at United after a spell in charge of the USMNT.

headline: Pochettino told 'Manchester is blue' and has a reply ready
facts: Ex-USMNT defender DeMarcus Beasley told Pochettino on TNT Sports US that Manchester is a blue city.
Pochettino disagreed and said fans would see otherwise, but that he needed time.
His United tenure officially began that Wednesday.
background: Pochettino coached the USMNT before United, which is why a former US international was interviewing him.

headline: Neil Warnock named 'Chief of Socks' and mocks holes-in-socks trend
facts: Warnock became 'Chief of Socks' for The Famous Grouse and modelled a limited Christmas sock range.
He criticised top players cutting holes in their socks, saying he does not believe it gives an advantage.
He draws on his chiropody qualifications for the role.
background: Kyle Walker said in 2021 he cut holes in his socks to release tension in his calves.

headline: Sneijder admits he 'released anger' at half-time of a legends charity game
facts: Sneijder played for Ajax legends against Barcelona legends at the Johan Cruyff Arena; Barcelona won 7-4.
He said he was only allowed about 30 minutes and criticised teammates and Danny Blind's selection.
The day before, he won his first game as manager of ninth-tier Eminent Boys 3-1.
background: Sneijder retired in 2019, and his last club was Al Gharafa.
footage_terms: Ajax legends Barcelona legends Johan Cruyff Arena

headline: Mudryk's loan podcast comments about Chelsea return go viral
facts: On a podcast Mudryk described Xabi Alonso telling him to get match time and come back to Chelsea.
Jamie O'Hara reacted angrily, saying Mudryk was using Tottenham as a stepping stone and should be sent back.
Sky Sports reports De Zerbi says he understands fan frustration and that Mudryk must show his qualities.
background: Chelsea loaned Mudryk to Tottenham in the summer, and he has played only once for Spurs after an ankle injury.

headline: Bebe, 'United's biggest ever flop', finds a club in Spain's third tier
facts: Bebe joined CD Teruel, bottom of Spain's third division, after months as a free agent.
He left UD Ibiza at the end of last season.
An ESPN fan survey once named him United's biggest ever flop.
background: Ferguson signed Bebe from Vitoria de Guimaraes in August 2010 for a reported 7.4 million pounds, and he made only seven United appearances in four years.

headline: Gareth Bale reportedly part of a bid group for Sevilla
facts: El Confidencial reported Bale advises US fund Juggernaut Capital Partners, one of three groups interested in Sevilla.
A rival group, HD Ventures, led by the Sayed brothers, is also reported to be interested.
This is a report, not a confirmed deal; Bale earlier failed in an attempt to buy Cardiff.
background: Bale retired in 2023 aged 33 after three seasons at Los Angeles FC, and has spent far more time on the golf course than the pitch.
footage_terms: Gareth Bale best goals Real Madrid

headline: Kane wants his Ballon d'Or displayed in the Bayern museum
facts: Kane told SportBILD he would ask Bayern about putting the Ballon d'Or in the club museum.
He collected the award on 26 October at the London Palladium, ahead of Mbappe by 28 points.
He also plans gifts for teammates at Bayern and England.
background: Kane is the first Englishman to win the Ballon d'Or since Michael Owen in 2001.

headline: Yamal's uncle slams Kane's Ballon d'Or win on Spanish radio
facts: Yamal's uncle Abdul Abdellaoui called the result sad on El Larguero and said Yamal is the best player in the world.
He argued fans come to watch Yamal rather than Kane and said voters held Yamal's age against him.
Final top three was Kane, Mbappe, Yamal.
background: Yamal also won the Kopa Trophy for best young player for a third straight year.
footage_terms: Harry Kane Ballon d'Or win reaction

headline: Yamal's father says 'Lamine Yamal' is not his real full name
facts: On a live broadcast, Mounir Nasraoui said Lamine Yamal is his son's first name, not a first name plus surname.
He gave the surname as Nasraoui Ebana.
He asked everyone to understand that.
background: Yamal is Barcelona's teenage winger, who finished third in the 2026 Ballon d'Or voting.

headline: Mbappe's Mao-meme joke angers China; CCTV pulls Real Madrid games
facts: On the French show The Bridge, Mbappe said his favourite meme of himself showed him as a Chinese dictator with his face on Mao.
Mbappe apologised, calling the comment ill-judged, and Chinese sponsors Dongpeng, Mengniu and Milkground ended partnerships with him.
China Media Group suspended Real Madrid broadcasts on CCTV-5 until the club formally apologises, and Real Madrid issued an apology.
background: China reportedly accounts for 10 to 15 percent of Real Madrid's international merchandise sales.

headline: Barcelona wear 'GOLF' on the shirt for El Clasico, Tyler, The Creator collab
facts: The word GOLF on the front promotes Tyler, The Creator's GOLF WANG brand in a Spotify campaign.
The shirt was for the El Clasico on 25 October, and only 1,899 matchday shirts were sold to the public.
Spotify gave an artist full creative control over a campaign for the first time.
background: Spotify has sponsored Barcelona since 2022, and past Clasico shirts have featured artists starting with Drake in 2022.
footage_terms: Barcelona Real Madrid El Clasico October 2026 highlights

headline: Harvey Elliott sent off for two yellows in seconds after arguing with the referee
facts: Elliott came on in the 70th minute and got two yellows within seconds after a row with the referee as Valencia lost 2-1 to Villarreal.
Valencia boss Javier Aguirre called it absurd and noted Elliott barely speaks Spanish.
Marca gave him 3.9 out of 10, and Valencia are 19th on six points from 10 games.
background: Elliott is a Liverpool player on loan at Valencia.
footage_terms: Harvey Elliott red card Valencia Villarreal

headline: Sancho offered about 10,000 pounds a week by Getafe
facts: Getafe president Angel Torres said the club made Sancho a final offer.
Reports put the wage near 10,000 pounds a week; the Telegraph figure was 400,000 euros until June.
Sancho has not ruled it out and wants to meet coach Jose Bordalas.
background: Sancho reportedly earned 250,000 pounds a week at Manchester United, and he is a free agent after his United contract ended in June.

headline: Strasbourg's Godo goes viral for odd pre-match eye routine, then scores
facts: Before kick-off Godo moved his fingers before his face, shifted his gaze and closed one eye repeatedly.
Strasbourg beat Auxerre 5-1, and it was Godo's first goal of the season.
He said the routine puts him in the conditions of reality.
background: Godo plays for Strasbourg in Ligue 1.

headline: Dortmund want Nmecha to drop his crown-removing goal celebration
facts: After a brace in a 2-1 win over Elversberg, Nmecha pointed up and placed an imaginary crown on the turf; four teammates joined in.
Fans objected to the Christian network Ballers in God over its reported views on homosexuality and abortion.
WDR reports Dortmund will ask the group not to use Nmecha and will urge him to stop; Nmecha says it honours Jesus and is not about hate.
background: Nmecha is a Germany international midfielder who plays for Dortmund.

headline: Teenager Dowman sent off vs Fleetwood; lip-reader claims Arteta's reaction
facts: Max Dowman, 16, was sent off in the 85th minute after reacting to a heavy challenge from Harrison Neal.
Arsenal drew 1-1 with 26 shots and 78% possession, then lost 5-3 on penalties to Fleetwood.
A lip-reader said Arteta told Dowman to go straight to the changing room; Arsenal fans criticised Arteta on social media.
background: Fleetwood are a lower-league side, and Arsenal were Carabao Cup round-of-16 favourites.

headline: Hincapie answers Van Dijk's sarcasm with 'I don't forget' Instagram post
facts: Arsenal won 1-0 at Anfield through a first-half Kai Havertz goal, their first win there since 2014.
Van Dijk said a penalty was clear on Isak after a Timber shirt pull, and sarcastically congratulated Arsenal.
Hincapie posted images captioned 'I don't forget', including a zoomed-in Premier League sleeve badge.
background: Van Dijk posted a similar sleeve-badge image after Liverpool's 0-0 draw at the Emirates in January.

headline: Henderson taps the Chelsea badge after scoring and Liverpool fans fume
facts: Chelsea beat Bournemouth 5-1; Henderson scored in the second minute and added a free kick in the 70th.
After the second goal he tapped the Chelsea badge, and some Liverpool fans called it disrespectful.
It was only his second Chelsea appearance.
background: Henderson, 36, joined Chelsea in the summer after his Brentford contract was mutually terminated, and some Liverpool fans saw the move as betrayal.

headline: Man City fans carry inflatable bananas in defiance after 115-charges verdict
facts: City fans are taking inflatable bananas to games after the club was found guilty of 115 charges by an independent commission.
Former striker Imre Varadi sells branded bananas for 10 pounds and says demand has gone through the roof.
The tradition dates to 1987, when Frank Newton brought one to a game against Plymouth.
background: The inflatable craze started in the 1987 season, long before the City ownership era.

headline: Liam Rosenior says Chelsea memes went too far: 'I'm not a joke'
facts: In So Foot, Rosenior said the media made his Chelsea tenure a joke, citing mockery of the note he gave Garnacho against PSG.
Chelsea sacked him on 22 April after 107 days, with 11 wins in 23 games.
He now manages Paris FC, with five wins and two draws from his first nine matches.
background: Rosenior had a short spell at Chelsea before returning to France.

headline: Iraola: Liverpool are 'too honest' as the referee praised their conduct after a loss
facts: Iraola said the referee complimented Liverpool players and staff after the 1-0 loss to Arsenal, and he was unsure how to feel.
He said Liverpool can be too honest about refereeing decisions.
Opta: Liverpool have been awarded only 88 fouls this season while conceding 128, the most in the league.
background: Iraola took over at Liverpool this season, following Arne Slot's sacking.

headline: Adidas launches knitted long-sleeve club shirts for Arsenal, Liverpool and Man Utd
facts: The knitted long-sleeve home shirts are a first for Adidas; Arsenal's version landed first in the UK.
The shirts replace the sponsor with the club name and have ribbed cuffs and waistband.
Liverpool and United versions are due before Christmas, with Real Madrid and Juventus expected too.
background: Knitwear shirts are limited to Adidas Elite clubs.

headline: Haaland bumps into childhood friend Andrea Norheim after winning goal at Leipzig
facts: Haaland met Norheim, now a Leipzig player, near the dressing room after City won 3-2 and he scored the winner.
They had not seen each other for about eight years.
Norheim said he recognised her immediately.
background: Both were youth teammates at Bryne FK in Norway.

headline: Southampton give Eckert a new deal despite the 'Spygate' scandal
facts: Eckert signed a new contract to 2029, 20 November, after Southampton admitted unauthorised filming of opponents' training before a play-off semi-final.
Southampton were expelled from the play-off final and docked four points; the FA gave Eckert a suspended six-week ban and a fine on 25 September.
Owner Dragan Solak said the suspended sentence let Eckert continue.
background: Middlesbrough complained on 7 May, and Hull City beat them in the play-off final.
